ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Frida Kahlo — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Adult preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Ms. Kahlo returns for an adult preventive visit, booked separately from her pain care. The cold she had two weeks ago cleared within ten days without antibiotics. One week ago her oxycodone was reduced from 60 to 52.5 MME a day, and she reports no withdrawal symptoms and pain she can manage, with a PEG of 5.7 today. She attends physical therapy twice a week and cognitive behavioral therapy weekly, and she has had no falls since starting care here. She received this season's influenza vaccine last week. She does not recall when she last had cervical cancer screening, and no result is on record. She explains that lying on an examination table with her legs raised aggravates her back and hip pain, so she would prefer to avoid a speculum examination if she can. She completed the health risk assessment before the visit. [S]

Adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and a written prevention plan given. Depression, anxiety, alcohol, drug use, tobacco, and personal-safety screens are negative. Blood pressure 114/70 mmHg is normal. [S]
Next preventive visit in one year.

Fall risk from right leg weakness and shortening after polio and the old fractures (B91). Raised: a Timed Up and Go of 14 seconds, a cane, and oxycodone and duloxetine, which can both cause dizziness. No falls since starting care here. [S]
Continue gait and balance training in physical therapy and wear the shoe lift.
Install bathroom grab bars and a rail on the courtyard steps; night lights on the route to the bathroom.
Avoid sedating medicines, including over-the-counter sleep aids and antihistamines.

Long-term opioid therapy on a gradual taper, 52.5 MME a day (Z79.891). One week after the first reduction she has no withdrawal symptoms and her function is holding. Storage is safe and naloxone is at home. [S]
No change today; the taper is reviewed at next week's scheduled visit.
If she ever plans a pregnancy or becomes pregnant, call before changing any medicine. Oxycodone should not be stopped suddenly, and her medicines would be reviewed together ahead of time.

Vitamin D deficiency (E55.9). On repletion; low bone-loading activity and the leg weakness add to bone risk. [S]
Continue cholecalciferol 2,000 units daily.
Recheck 25-hydroxyvitamin D about three months after starting.
